chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Why Max Roach and Miles Davis dislike the word jazz
summary: Gil explains that Max wants recognition for his knowledge and that Miles said the word reminds him of whiskey and cigarettes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: If you have a person like Max for example, who wants it to be known, actually what Max wants is for people to know how much he knows, which
he does. He's an accomplished artist, you know. He knows so much about music that it just irks him I guess, you know, to be labeled.
Yes, and it could conceivably cut down on his income. You know, in order to get a job that pays him good money (?).
That's what he says. I've heard him say that.

Other people don't like it because it reminds them of whiskey and cigarettes, you know. I think Miles Davis said that once. He said he didn't want to hear the word jazz anymore because that reminded him of whiskey and cigarettes which he didn't like.
